text:
Devon Park: Postmortem follow-up: pattern identified = intermittent host OOMs leading to abrupt stream termination -> clients retry quickly -> connection churn (reconnect storm) -> many sessions report 1-2 partial chunks before final disconnect. Need prioritized actions with owners and short timelines.

Nina Zhou: I'll take ownership of the memory OOM investigation across the GPU host pool. Plan: collect heap dumps, correlate with model load/unload cycles, and run a 6-hour soak on a small canary. ETA: initial findings 24h.

Raj Patel: I'll handle load-balancer behaviour and session affinity. Hypothesis: affinity timeouts shorter than client's streaming TTL causing stickiness flips under host recycling. I'll produce a config diff and a canary rollback plan by tomorrow morning.

Alice Chen: I'll coordinate rollout gating and customer comms. Also want a pragmatic interim mitigation: throttle client reconnect attempts server-side and drop immediate retries that occur within 500ms. Could be a quick config toggle.

Devon Park: Ops bot snapshot: 2024-09-12T04:12Z incident - 8 affected customers, spike in partial-responses at 03:58-04:05Z, per-region burst on us-east-1. Reconnect_count median=2.

Nina Zhou: Notes on probing: prefer capturing tracing headers using x-request-id so we can join client logs. Will add ephemeral tracing to canary.

Raj Patel: Proposed quick LB changes:
```
- session_affinity_ttl: 120s -> 300s
- healthcheck_grace: 10s -> 30s
- treat_302_as_unhealthy: true
```
I'll stage these in two edge pools and run traffic canary at 5% for 1 hour.

Alice Chen: Runtime change proposal from me: add server-side reconnect throttle config. Example pseudo-config:
```
streaming:
  reconnect_throttle_ms: 500
  max_reconnects_per_session: 6
  reconnect_jitter_ms: 200
```
This should reduce reconnect storms while longer-term fixes land.

Devon Park: Action list (who/what/when):
- OOM root cause + canary -> Nina (24h)
- LB affinity + healthcheck changes -> Raj (config + canary 36h)
- Server-side throttle toggle -> Alice (PR + small rollout 24-48h)
- Observability slices -> Devon (alert + dashboard changes in 12h)
- Customer one-pager -> Alice (draft 48h after mitigation plan)

ops-bot: Log extract: partial_chunk_rate=3.8% at peak, reconnect_rate=1.6% peak, median_time_between_reconnects=420ms.

Devon Park: Observability asks: per-session reconnect histogram, partial-chunk index (which chunk number was partial), and client ttl expiries. I'll spike an ad-hoc Grafana panel and a high-cardinality log query for today.

Nina Zhou: Update 2210450302: Captured heap samples from canary host. Initial smell: model shard cleanup sometimes delayed during eviction, causing temporary memory pressure. I'm scheduling a runtime patch to speed shard GC and will test.

Raj Patel: Update 2210450600: Config diff ready -> /infra/proposals/lb-affinity-2210450600.diff. Starting 5% canary in pool-a at 10:30 UTC. Monitoring will be on the staging dashboard.

Alice Chen: Update 2210450899: I opened a small feature flag to throttle reconnects -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4340. It's behind a feature flag named reconnect_throttle_v1. Please review; will run unit + integration tests.

Devon Park: Update 2210451189: dashboard tile up with new metric slices. Early canary telemetry shows partials down ~25% and reconnects down ~40% in the canary pool. Good sign. We'll extend canary if numbers hold.

Alice Chen: Next sync: same thread tomorrow at 10:00 UTC. If canary looks clean we'll plan a staggered prod rollout and customer comms. Keep updates short in-thread. :thumbsup:
